class.name: VoxelGenerator
class.brief_description: The ground a [VoxelTerrain3D] starts with, before anyone digs into it.
class.description: Describes the ground everywhere a voxel terrain has not been edited, so the world can be as large as the view distance without storing it. The ground has a surface height, made of a flat [member height], [member height_noise] for hills, and [member height_source] to start from an existing heightmap terrain. Under the surface, [member cave_noise] carves caves. All distances here are in metres. Changing a setting rebuilds the terrain; voxels that have already been edited keep their values.

method.name: get_surface_height
method.description: Returns the height of the generated ground at [param x], [param z], in metres relative to the terrain's origin.

members.member: The deepest below the surface caves go, in metres. Everything deeper is solid rock, which is also what lets the terrain skip building blocks far underground.
How far below the surface caves start, in metres. At [code]0.0[/code] caves can open onto the surface.

Carves caves where its value is above [member cave_threshold]. A [FastNoiseLite] with a frequency around [code]0.02[/code] to [code]0.05[/code] gives winding caves a few metres wide. Leave empty for solid ground.
How much of the noise becomes cave: lower values carve bigger, more connected caves.
The layer of the ground more than [member deep_layer_depth] below the surface, and of cave walls.
How deep, in metres, the surface layer goes before the deep layer starts. Digging a pit shows the change.
The height of the ground, in metres, where nothing else sets it.
How far, in metres, [member height_noise] raises and lowers the ground.
Adds hills and valleys, [member height_amplitude] metres up and down. Leave empty for flat ground.

Takes the ground's height, and the layers painted on it, from a heightmap terrain's data, so a landscape made with [Terrain3D] becomes the base for caves and overhangs. Outside its regions, [member height] applies. Its layer indices are used as they are, so give the voxel terrain the same layers; the Terrain dock's Convert to Voxel Terrain does all of this.
Where the heightmap terrain sits relative to the voxel terrain, in metres.
The layer of the ground near the surface, where [member height_source] does not say otherwise.
